sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: On a summer afternoon, the centre of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the farmland a few kilometres beyond its edge. This phenomenon, known as the urban heat island, arises because concrete, asphalt and brick absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly through the night, while the trees and open soil that would have cooled the air through evaporation have been paved over. Waste heat from vehicles, air conditioners and industry adds to the burden. The consequences are not merely a matter of discomfort. Nights that fail to cool deprive the body of its chance to recover, and heat-related illness falls most heavily on the elderly, outdoor labourers and residents of crowded settlements with tin roofs and little ventilation.

Paradoxically, the most common private response deepens the problem. Every air conditioner that cools a room expels heat into the street outside, so that relief purchased by those who can afford it is partly paid for by those who cannot. Lasting remedies are therefore collective rather than individual: reflective roofs, shaded pedestrian streets, protected water bodies and a deliberate expansion of tree cover. Such measures are modest in cost compared with the hospital admissions and lost working days that a hotter city quietly accumulates each year. A city that plans for shade, in short, plans for the health of its poorest citizens.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: When self-help groups first spread through rural India, they were celebrated as a means of bringing credit to women whom banks had never considered worth the paperwork. A dozen women would meet weekly, pool small savings and lend to one another, and once the group had proven its discipline, a bank would extend a larger loan to it collectively. Repayment rates were remarkably high, for each member's reputation among her neighbours stood behind the debt. Many women used their first loans to buy a goat, a sewing machine or stock for a small shop, and some gained for the first time a measure of say in household decisions.

Success, however, attracted imitators less interested in empowerment than in profit. In several regions, commercial lenders competed to sign up borrowers, extending multiple loans to the same household at high rates of interest and enforcing repayment through public shaming. Debt that had once been a ladder became, for some, a trap. The lesson is not that small loans are harmful but that credit is a tool, not a cure. Without savings, training, access to markets and some protection against illness or crop failure, a loan merely transfers risk to those least able to bear it. The original groups worked because they were built on mutual trust; the mere imitation of their form could not reproduce it.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most suitable title for the passage?
opts: Concrete: The Ideal Material for Hot Climates
Heat in the City: A Shared Problem Needing Shared Remedies
The Rising Price of Air Conditioners
Why Farmland Is Warmer Than Cities at Night
questions.why: Main idea: the passage explains the urban heat island and concludes that 'lasting remedies are therefore collective rather than individual'.

questions.q: According to the passage, why do nights in the city centre fail to cool?
opts: Winds from the farmland are blocked by tall buildings.
Evaporation from trees warms the air after sunset.
Built surfaces release the heat absorbed during the day slowly through the night.
Vehicles and industry produce more heat at night than by day.
questions.why: Detail: 'concrete, asphalt and brick absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly through the night'.

questions.q: It can be inferred that the author regards private air-conditioning as a response that:
opts: is the main reason farmland is cooler than cities.
shifts part of the heat burden onto people who cannot afford relief.
has no effect on temperatures outside the home.
is the most effective long-term remedy for urban heat.
questions.why: Inference: 'relief purchased by those who can afford it is partly paid for by those who cannot', because each unit 'expels heat into the street outside'.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards measures such as tree cover and shaded streets is best described as:
opts: approving, seeing them as cost-effective investments in public health.
dismissive, treating them as merely cosmetic.
sceptical, doubting that their cost can be justified.
neutral, offering no view on their worth.
questions.why: Tone: such measures are 'modest in cost compared with the hospital admissions and lost working days', and 'a city that plans for shade... plans for the health of its poorest citizens'.

questions.q: As used in the passage, the word 'Paradoxically' means:
opts: gradually and over a long period
in a way that seems contrary to what one would expect
in a way that is fortunate for everyone
in a way that is easy to predict
questions.why: Vocabulary: a cooling device that 'deepens the problem' of heat is a seemingly contradictory outcome.

questions.q: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
opts: Commercial lenders improved on the self-help group model.
Banks should stop lending to self-help groups.
Small loans are always harmful to poor households.
Group credit empowered rural women when built on trust and support, but profit-driven imitation made it harmful for some.
questions.why: Main idea: the original groups 'worked because they were built on mutual trust', while imitators 'less interested in empowerment than in profit' turned debt into 'a trap'.

questions.q: According to the passage, why were repayment rates in the early groups high?
opts: Banks charged very high rates of interest.
Lenders used public shaming to enforce repayment.
Each member's reputation among her neighbours stood behind the debt.
questions.why: Detail: 'for each member's reputation among her neighbours stood behind the debt'.

questions.q: The statement 'Debt that had once been a ladder became, for some, a trap' suggests that:
opts: credit that once helped women advance came to confine some borrowers in hardship.
borrowers used loans to buy ladders and tools.
all borrowers were eventually trapped by debt.
debt has never helped anyone improve their position.
questions.why: Inference: a ladder enables climbing; a trap holds one fast. The words 'for some' rule out 'all borrowers'.

questions.q: The author's stance on small loans is best described as:
opts: entirely hostile to all forms of small loans.
balanced, valuing the original model while criticising its profit-driven imitation.
indifferent to the outcome for borrowers.
questions.why: Tone: 'The lesson is not that small loans are harmful but that credit is a tool, not a cure.'

questions.q: As used in the passage, 'a measure of say' means:
opts: an official position in the village
questions.why: Vocabulary: some women gained 'a measure of say in household decisions', i.e. a share of influence over them.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “She ____ tea every morning.”
questions.why: A habitual action takes the simple present. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A person who hates mankind”
questions.why: A misanthrope dislikes and distrusts people in general. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The patient's fever has not ____ even after three days.”
questions.why: 'Come down' means to decrease, as of a fever. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: He said, I will come tomorrow.”
questions.why: A comma introduces the direct speech, which is enclosed in quotation marks. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the correctly spelt word:
questions.why: The only English word ending in -sede (with no other -cede form). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang, placed on UNESCO's tentative list in October 2026, is in:
questions.why: Listed with the Andaman Subduction Volcanoes (Barren and Narcondam). Oct 2026.

questions.q: Sawan Barwal won silver at the 2026 Asian Games, India's first medal in his event since 1982. What was the event?
questions.why: The Army runner ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games marathon medal. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Exercise MAITREE-XV, held at Surat Thani from 18 to 31 August 2026, is an army exercise between India and:
questions.why: It focuses on counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations. Aug 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was renamed:
questions.why: Cabinet continued it for FY27 to FY31 and renamed its pension sub-schemes. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which team won the Duleep Trophy in September 2026, beating South Zone on first-innings lead?
questions.why: Captain Ishan Kishan scored a double hundred in the final at Chennai. Sep 2026.

questions.q: According to Amit Shah in Panaji (September 2026), Goa ranked where in the country in implementing the new criminal laws?
questions.why: He cited a 93.38% performance rate. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Kala Academy building at Campal, Panaji, was designed by:
questions.why: It is Goa's main centre for the performing arts.

questions.q: In August 2026, Jos Buttler became the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket history by overtaking:
questions.why: Buttler passed the record while playing in The Hundred. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Goa's common civil code, which applies to all communities, comes from the Portuguese Civil Code of:
questions.why: It was extended to Goa in 1870 and kept after Liberation.

questions.q: Ahmedabad airport became the third airport under India's international hub-and-spoke model in September 2026, after Varanasi and:
questions.why: Air India's Easy Connect lets passengers clear customs at Ahmedabad before flying abroad via Delhi. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Rahul is 23rd from the top and 23rd from the bottom in a class. How many students are in the class?
questions.why: Total = 23 + 23 − 1 = 45. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:00?
questions.why: Angle = |30×3 − 5.5×0| = 90°. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Sita walks 5 m East, then turns left and walks 8 m, then turns left and walks 9 m. Which direction is Sita facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the West. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Pointing to a woman, Asha (a man) said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the woman related to Asha?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Sister. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If 19 October 2025 was a Sunday, what day of the week was 16 November 2025?
questions.why: 28 days later; 28 mod 7 = 0, so count 0 days on from Sunday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 14, 20, 29, 41, 56, …
questions.why: The differences go up by 3 each time (6, 9, 12, 15, 18). Next: 74. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a row of 34 students, Ravi is 6th from the left and Asha is 18th from the right. How many students sit between them?
questions.why: Between them = 34 − (6 + 18) = 10. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Sita walks 7 m South, then turns right and walks 9 m, then turns left and walks 4 m, then turns left and walks 6 m. Which direction is Sita facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the East. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a group of 80 people, 51 like cricket, 26 like football and 20 like neither. How many like only cricket?
questions.why: Both = 51 + 26 − (80 − 20) = 17; only cricket = 51 − 17 = 34. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The present ages of Ravi and Anil are in the ratio 6 : 2. After 3 years the ratio will be 51 : 19. What is Anil's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 6k and 2k: (6k + 3)/(2k + 3) = 51/19 gives k = 8, so Anil is 16. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: According to §2, the highest ideal of cure is:
opts: removal of the most troublesome symptom as quickly as possible
palliation of suffering until the disease runs its natural course
removal of the material cause of disease by evacuation
rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health on easily comprehensible principles
questions.why: §2 defines the ideal cure as rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health, or removal of the disease in its whole extent, in the shortest, most reliable and most harmless way.

questions.q: According to §141, the best of all provings are those made by:
opts: the healthy, unprejudiced and sensitive physician on himself
students under the supervision of a professor
volunteers who know nothing of the drug
questions.why: §141: the best pure experiments are those the healthy, unprejudiced, sensitive physician makes on himself.

questions.q: Carbo vegetabilis is prepared from:
questions.why: Carbo vegetabilis is wood (vegetable) charcoal; Carbo animalis is animal charcoal, Spongia roasted sponge and Calcarea carb the middle layer of the oyster shell.

questions.q: Skin eruptions with deep, bleeding cracks that are worse in winter, together with seasickness, point to:
questions.why: Petroleum: deep fissures and cracks worse in winter; nausea from riding in carriages and ships (Boericke).

questions.q: A fever patient who must be covered in every stage, because he becomes chilly on the slightest uncovering or movement even during the heat, needs:
questions.why: Nux vomica: chilliness in all stages of fever; cannot move or uncover without feeling chilly (Allen's Keynotes).

questions.q: After soaking in the potency, medicated globules should be dried:
opts: in the shade, away from sunlight and strong heat
questions.why: Heat and sunlight can damage the medicine, so medicated globules are dried in shade at room temperature.

questions.q: The manner of labelling homoeopathic medicines is laid down specifically in Rule:
questions.why: Rule 106-A governs the labelling of homoeopathic medicines; Rules 96 and 97 deal with labelling of other drugs and Rule 65 with conditions of retail licences.

questions.q: The word 'repertory' comes from the Latin 'repertorium', meaning:
opts: a storehouse, a place where things can be found
questions.why: A repertorium is a storehouse or inventory, an index from which symptoms and remedies can be retrieved.

questions.q: Kent regarded menstrual symptoms as:
questions.why: Kent held that menstrual state expresses the woman as a whole, so he ranked menstrual symptoms as generals.

questions.q: In the liver, bilirubin is made water-soluble by conjugation with:
questions.why: UDP-glucuronyl transferase conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid; albumin only carries unconjugated bilirubin in plasma.

questions.q: Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus endangers the:
questions.why: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck with the posterior circumflex humeral vessels.

questions.q: Tall, peaked T waves on the ECG are characteristic of:
questions.why: Raised potassium speeds repolarisation and produces tall tented T waves; hypokalaemia gives flat T waves and U waves.

questions.q: Kerley B lines on a chest X-ray indicate:
questions.why: Kerley B lines are short horizontal lines at the lung bases from fluid-thickened interlobular septa, as in left ventricular failure.

questions.q: Excessive scar tissue that grows beyond the margins of the original wound and does not regress is called a:
questions.why: A keloid extends beyond the wound boundary and seldom regresses; a hypertrophic scar stays within the wound margins.

questions.q: Fever with rigors, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain (Charcot's triad) indicate:
questions.why: Charcot's triad reflects infection of an obstructed common bile duct; adding confusion and hypotension gives Reynolds' pentad.

questions.q: Urticaria is termed chronic when wheals recur for more than:
questions.why: Urticaria lasting more than 6 weeks is chronic; second-generation H1 antihistamines are the first-line drugs.

questions.q: Under the Rome IV criteria, IBS requires recurrent abdominal pain on average at least:
opts: 3 days per month in the last 3 months
1 day per week in the last 3 months
Once a month for a year
questions.why: Rome IV: pain at least 1 day a week for 3 months, with symptom onset at least 6 months before, linked to defecation or change in stool frequency or form; '3 days per month' was Rome III.

questions.q: Carcinoma of the cervix is most strongly associated with infection by:
questions.why: High-risk HPV 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers.

questions.q: In active management of the third stage of labour, the uterotonic of choice is:
opts: ergometrine 0.5 mg IV before delivery of the shoulder
misoprostol 1000 mcg rectally after the placenta
oxytocin 10 IU IM within one minute of birth
questions.why: WHO and Indian guidelines recommend oxytocin 10 IU IM as the first-choice uterotonic for AMTSL.

questions.q: The earliest clinical sign of rickets in a young infant is:
questions.why: Craniotabes (ping-pong softening of the skull) appears in early infancy; rosary and limb deformities come later.

questions.q: A rodent ulcer is a:
questions.why: Rodent ulcer is the common name for basal cell carcinoma, which locally erodes tissue.

questions.q: Sinusitis with thick, tough, stringy, yellow-green discharge and pain at the root of the nose calls for:
questions.why: Ropy, stringy discharge with pressure pain at the root of the nose is the keynote of Kali bichromicum.

questions.q: After a snakebite, blood that fails to clot in the 20-minute whole blood clotting test indicates envenomation by a:
questions.why: Viper venom is haemotoxic and causes coagulopathy; cobra and krait venoms are neurotoxic.

questions.q: The ethical principle expressed as 'primum non nocere' is:
questions.why: Primum non nocere ('first, do no harm') is the principle of non-maleficence.

questions.q: The Nalgonda technique is used for:
opts: removal of excess fluoride from drinking water
questions.why: Developed by NEERI, the Nalgonda technique uses alum and lime to defluoridate water; fluoride above 1.5 mg/L causes fluorosis.
